chapter: Hartford, prison, theater and the Collective
title: Why the Collective teaches many arts: saving youth
summary: McLean offered music, dance and visual arts to save youth and give direction; Eric LaSalle took his first drama lessons there.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Why multi-disciplines? What’s the theory behind that.

I just thought it would be – it would offer the kids more to choose from, basically, rather than to say, we’re starting a music school. Maybe everybody don’t want to be bothered with music. So music and dance, the visual arts.
Was your motivation to develop artists or to save youth?

To save youth and to give youth some direction. And at the same time – Eric LaSalle is the other guy I was trying to think of yesterday, the guy that’s on Emergency Room, the brother on that show. He started here at the Collective, took his first drama lessons here. So we were serious about doing both things, saving the youth, giving them some direction, but at the same time, trying to draw out some talent and give kids some options.
